newsitem.title: CHINA: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Hutchison bond could be upped.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Hutchison bond could be upped.

text.p: The planned US$1 billion global bond by Hutchison Whampoa Ltd could be increased even before its launch, market sources said on Monday.
Commenting on speculation it might be as high as US$2 billion, one banker close to the deal said "US$1.5 billion sounds reasonable, US$2 billion sounds pretty high."
Arrangers are Merrill Lynch and Goldman Sachs. Co-managers are HSBC, J.P. Morgan, Peregrine Fixed Income and UBS.
The four-tranche deal -- it will have 10-year, 20-year, 30-year and 40-year tranches -- will be launched this week,
Also rumoured to be coming to the market with a U.S. dollar deal is Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd, which sources said may be considering a US$300 million 144a placement.
More terms have emerged on the Cheung Kong Infrastructure HK$3.8 billion loan/revolving credit.
The deal includes a covenant that Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd will maintain 35 percent direct or indirect ownership of Hong Kong Electric Co Ltd.
The underwriting fee is 3 basis points for HK$$250 million, and co-arranging fee is nine basis points.
Responses are due by late July.
Continued selling of some Asian emerging market currencies is likely to put a dampener on Asian debt this week, with Indonesia feeling the pinch this time.
Indonesia's central bank intervened in the foreign exchange market to sell U.S. dollar forwards outright after speculative offshore attacks on the rupiah.
"But the overall appetite for dollars remains strong," one dealer said. "There are still attempts to test the (intervention) band."
A combination of more Asian currency speculation and testimony by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan is likely to keep Asian debt investors and issuers sidelined this week.
Analysts said Greenspan might indicate that expectations that the latest round of Fed tightening was over were misplaced, citing strong U.S. economic growth.
A major Thai financial institution is rumoured to have pulled out of a planned US$100 million FRCD, sources said.
If true, it would be the latest in a series of Thai financial institutions or corporates to either pull an issue or re-price it in recent months.
One veteran arranger of Thai offshore deals said top names can still raise cash, although second-tier borrowers are likely to find it more difficult.

In a new blow to Thailand's battered banking sector, Moody's Investors Service cut ratings of Bangkok Metropolitan Bank, cutting its ratings for long-term bank deposits and senior debt to Baa3 (from Ba1).
Standard & Poor's also rated Krungthai Thanakit Public Co Ltd (KTT), warning that the outlook was negative.
Krungthai Thanakit Public Co Ltd (KTT) received BBB-minus long-term and A-3 short-term counterparty ratings.
